_about: What a person read by eye on the two pictures (2 Nov 2026), in picture pixels (x right, y down), approximate: read_pictures.py measures each of these on the pixels (wall ends, faces, tread lines, blobs) and writes the exact result to takeoff.json. Words (room names, kinds, families) cannot be measured: they are typed here as read. Keys that start with '_' are notes.

F1._picture: Floor 1 (the owner, 2 Nov: the first picture is floor 1).
F1._area: Where walls are read: the building, the RED BOX vestibule and the stair bay. Outside it are traffic arrows, the dashed site lines, the red callouts and the frame of the sheet.
F1._liftDoors: Each lift door is the gap between two wall nibs on the lobby side of the core; measured on the columns x[0]..x[1] (inside the nibs, near their lobby face) between y[0] and y[1].
F1._core: Faces of the lift core measured on a grey-level profile (the first crossing of the half-way grey, 'down' = into the wall). The same names on floor 2 pair up: they give the scale between the pictures and the alignment.

width._: the clear width between the two brown side walls (the owner's 2.50 m, the scale's reference, rule 11): each inner face is the first stroke met coming from the stair (from x[0] towards x[1]); rows in the bay and below the red 'Luggage storage' box, which is drawn on the inner faces, clear of tread lines and of the break line

stairs._: UP arrow pointing north; the flight passes the north wall line into a bay between two brown side walls and rises to floor 2, where the picture of floor 2 shows its upper end as the open stair in the middle of the floor (F2-S2): the top riser is put on that edge.

plateClose.why: the stair leaves the building through the north wall line: the floor stops on that line

forecourt.why: the beige paving outside the south facade, from the building's west face (px 145) to its east face (px 1243) and south to the road at px y 733, where the traffic arrows start: an outdoor floor at 0.00 (assumed), so that the RED BOX's outer doors open onto floor; the thin rounded line at px y 705 is a line in the paving (the RED BOX itself reaches it), not its edge. The building's inside is taken out of it (rule 9).

south._: west of px x 800: further east a dark site band runs just below the line (px y 918-930)

aboveOutline._: Floor 1 dashes the outline of the floor above on the ground outside: a west line, a south line, and south of a wrap line it runs out east of the building (px 1243) to an east line. Each is measured as the median of the dashes' stroke centres (rule 12); build_model takes floor 2's terrace to it.

F2._glazing: The bar's side to the outdoor terrace is a thin double line with a light fill (grey 155-162 between two dark lines, 8 px): read as a glass screen. The west facade is a double line with a darker fill (130-140) with the MURAL WALL and the SIGNATURE CABINETS against it: read as wall.

width._: the clear width between the stair's two side walls (rule 11, as floor 1's flight, not a reference): each inner face is the first stroke met coming from the stair, on rows between the tread lines; the steps are built between them (build_model rule 6)

stairs._: UP arrow pointing north: the owner (2 Nov): this stair goes up to a floor 3 that is not drawn. Its 8 tread lines (the risers) are built as solid steps rising north from floor 2 between the enclosure's walls, ending in the air at the 8th line (rule 6); the grey landing north of them is left at floor 2's level, where the FEMALE door F2-006 opens.

width._: a check of the scale (rule 11): the iconic staircase between its stringers, as floor 2 draws it; the east stringer's inner line is lost in a shadow, so it is taken as wide as the west one

stairs._: The stair from floor 1 seen from above (drawn darker, 'UP.' and an arrow at its north end): the owner (2 Nov): the middle stair goes down to floor 1. Floor 2 is open over floor 1's flight, with railings on three sides; its north end is where the stair arrives. The void is fitted to floor 1's flight (build_model rule 6).
OUTSIDE STAIR: drawn faintly (thin vertical lines); 'UP.' with an arrow east and back west: a stair up to a floor not in the pictures, drawn as flat tread lines.
